items.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I was listening to: Bing Crosby, Frank Sinatra and oh the Condon group was going, and Nat King Cole I loved

ctx.x: Did you ever envision when you were let’s say in your early teens, did you get into rock & roll at all? Were you into the pop music of the day?

No I wasn’t. I grew up in the 50s and I went to college in ‘56 through ‘60. And I never liked it then. There were some tunes, there were some things I liked, some of the simple things. But for whatever reason, there was too much other going on I was listening to: Bing Crosby, Frank Sinatra and oh the Condon group was going, and Nat King Cole I loved and Doris Day. And I mean there were so many singers out there, and so many great groups, and so much other stuff happening with the big bands were still going a…
I’m picturing your college roommates maybe. Did they get into what you were — or were able to find some compatriots?
